Invokes the stored callable with this suite, surrounded by reporter calls to begin and end the suite. While the body runs, this suite is marked, in the runner, as the one that accepts new test cases (see accepts_test_case()); the previous one is restored when the body returns, also when it throws.

While the test cases are listed (see runner_options::list_tests), the body is called only to create its test cases, which are listed; the suite is neither reported nor timed, and an exception that escapes the body is reported by reject_body_exception(), on stderr and in the listing, the exit code is not 0, and the listing continues with the next suite.

When exceptions are enabled, an exception that escapes the callable, which can be thrown only outside the test cases, since they catch their own exceptions, is caught and reported as a failed check of this suite, and the suite ends normally, so that the run continues with the next suite; the test cases run before the exception remain reported, and the following ones are not run. A body declared noexcept cannot pass the exception on; the program is then terminated before it reaches this function.
As for the test cases, an exception thrown by the abort handler is passed on, without reporting it, and without ending the suite.

briefdescription.para: Adds a test case to the suite, and runs it.

detaileddescription.para:
Callable_T
The type of a callable object.
Args_T
The types of the callable arguments.
name
The test case name or description, used in reports; a string literal, a const char*, a std::string, or a std::string_view, converted implicitly to located_name, which copies it and also captures the location of the call.
callable
A generic callable object, usually a lambda, invoked to perform the test.
arguments
A possibly empty list of arguments to be passed to the callable.
Returns
Nothing.
The test function template creates a test case (a test_case with nesting depth 1) and runs it immediately. It accepts a descriptive name, a callable object (such as a lambda or function pointer), and an optional list of arguments to be passed to the callable, after the leading test_case& reference. The test case is reported using the provided name.

The test case is created and run by create_test_case(), as a local object destroyed when it returns, together with its stored body and bound arguments; only the number of test cases is kept, for the TAP plan.

Each test case typically involves evaluating logical expressions, such as comparing a computed result to an expected value, with expect() or require(). When exceptions are enabled, it is also possible to verify whether evaluating an expression throws exceptions. Each check either passes or fails, and the suite totals count the passed and failed checks.

It is typically invoked within the body of a suite. When invoked from the body of a running test case of this suite (for example via a captured suite reference), the new test case could not be reported as a sibling of the running one, which has not ended; it is therefore created by the innermost running test case, with test_case::test(), and runs nested in it, as if test() had been called on that test case.

The test case can be created only on the suite whose body is running. A call on another suite (for example on the top suite, captured by reference, from the body of a suite added with runner::add_suite(), or on any suite after runner::run_suites() returned) is rejected: the test case is not run, a failure is reported in the running suite, or, when none runs, an error is written to stderr, and the later calls of runner::run_suites() return a non-zero exit code.
Never called; the compilation stops in detail::reject_test_body(), with a message that names the mistake.

Each test case is named after the common name, followed by the value in parentheses, written as in the messages of the checks (Sizes (16)); a value that cannot be written (see extension::printable), such as an application type without an operator<<, is replaced by its position, starting at 1 (Records (#2)). The location of all the test cases is that of the call.

It is incremented for each check (by the check result) and for each nested test case created.

briefdescription.para: Checks whether a test case can be created on a suite.

detaileddescription.para: Protected, since it is used only by suite::test(). A test case can be created only on the suite whose body is running (the top suite, between runner::add_top_suite() and runner::run_suites(), or the suite being run). A call on any other suite, for example on the top suite from the body of another suite, on a static suite before the runner was initialised, or after runner::run_suites() returned, would run the test case where its results cannot be reported correctly. Such a call is rejected: the failure is reported as a failed check of the running test case, if one runs, otherwise in the running suite, or, when no suite runs, on stderr, and the rejection is remembered by the runner, which makes the exit code non-zero. When the session was declined (option errors, or --help), or aborted, the test cases are ignored silently, as after_test_case_create() ignores them.

target
The suite on which the test case is created.
name
The name and the location of the test case, for the message.
true
The test case can be created.
false
The test case must not be created.
The suite whose body runs accepts the test case. When the session was declined, or aborted, the test case is ignored, as after_test_case_create() ignores it.

Otherwise the call is rejected. If a test case runs (and the test cases are not only listed), the failure is reported as a check of that test case, so that it stays in its report. Otherwise, if a suite runs, the failure is reported as a check of that suite, with the same numbering and counting as the unexpected exceptions of the suite body. Otherwise (the runner was not initialised, has not started the suites, or has finished them, or the test cases are listed) the failure is given to runner::reject_call(), which writes the message on stderr and, where the reporter can still write it, as a comment line, for example in the list, and runner::mark_rejected() makes the exit code non-zero, as for the suites added too late.

briefdescription.para: Counts a newly constructed child test case and executes it immediately.

detaileddescription.para: The child test case is a local object of create_test_case(), and is destroyed when that function returns.

test_case
The newly created test_case.
suite
The parent suite to which execution results are reported.
Returns
Nothing.
Counts test_case, which is a local object of the calling create_test_case(), and immediately invokes test_case::run() on it. The test case is not kept; only child_test_cases_count_ is needed later, for the TAP plan.

If the filter patterns do not select the test case (its own name at its nesting level, or the name of suite at level 0, which matters only for the top suite, since the other suites run only when selected), its body is not called: the reporter is notified with skip_test_case() and the parent's skipped test cases counter is incremented. The test case keeps its index and its place among the children, so the TAP plan of the parent remains complete.

Otherwise, while the test case runs, the runner keeps it as its innermost running test case (see suite::test()). The parent's executed test cases counter is incremented after the run, and, if the child failed (a failed check, or a failed nested test case), its failed test cases counter too, so that the parent fails as well, as in node-tap. The child's check counters are intentionally not merged into the parent totals; each test case reports only its own counters. The child's totals are, however, accumulated into suite so that the suite summary reflects all checks performed by its test cases.
While the test cases are listed (see runner_options::list_tests), the selected test case is listed by the runner, and neither run nor counted, except in child_test_cases_count_.

After the test execution was aborted (possible only when the abort handler threw an exception, which the application caught), the report is complete, so the test case is neither run nor reported. The same applies when the runner refused to run the tests because of errors in the options, or because the output file could not be opened (see runner::has_option_errors()), or because the options requested the usage (--help).

memberdef.name: create_test_case

briefdescription.para: Creates a child test case, and runs it.

detaileddescription.para: The common body of suite::test() and test_case::test(), which differ only in the parent suite and the nesting depth of the test cases they create.
Always inlined into them, even without optimisations, since each nested test case adds one call chain to the stack, and a separate frame for this function would make it longer.

The test case runs and ends within the call, so, without additional arguments, it refers to the callable of the caller, which is neither copied nor moved, and is called in place, so a callable that cannot be copied is accepted, and an lvalue callable keeps the changes of its state. With additional arguments, the callable and the arguments are bound into a body of copies, by bind_callable().

Callable_T
The type of a callable object.
Args_T
The types of the callable arguments.
name
The test case name or description, used in reports, and the location of the call to test().
parent_suite
The suite to which the test case belongs.
nesting_depth
The depth of nesting of the test case; 1 for the direct children of a suite.
callable
A generic callable object, usually a lambda, invoked to perform the test.
arguments
A possibly empty list of arguments to be passed to the callable.
Returns
Nothing.
Without additional arguments, the child test_case is a local object that refers to the callable of the caller, which is neither copied nor moved, and is called in place (an lvalue callable keeps the changes of its state). A function is referred to through its pointer, and the callable and the additional arguments are bound into a local body, as copies, when there are arguments. The child is constructed with the next test point number of this node as its index, then passed to after_test_case_create(), which counts and runs it.

The child test case and its body, with the copies of the arguments, are destroyed when this function returns, so the memory used by a test session does not grow with the number of test cases; the stack holds one test case and one body for each level of nesting being run. Since the body is not stored in a std::function, it is never allocated, whatever the size of the lambda captures and of the arguments.

briefdescription.para: A named, runnable test suite registered with the test runner.

detaileddescription.para: suite represents a top-level named group of related test cases within the µTest++ framework. It is created by calling runner::add_suite(), which constructs the object and stores it in the runner's collection; the stored suites are run later by runner::run_suites(), together with the static suites, sorted by name. Each suite records its own timing information and propagates its results to the owning runner.

The suites to be run, registered or static, are kept in a single list, sorted by name, which does not depend on the runner object: its head is a constinit pointer, initialised before any constructor runs, and the links are members of the suites. The list includes the suites of all runners; each runner runs those that refer to it, in the order of the list.

The body of a suite is supplied as a callable (typically a lambda) that receives a suite& reference as its first argument. Inside the body, suite::test() is called to create and run individual test cases.

The constructor is private, since a suite constructed elsewhere would not be registered with the runner; the suites are created only by runner::add_suite(), by the derived static_suite, which registers itself, and by the runner, for its top_suite. The class is not meant to be derived from by the applications: top_suite and static_suite are its only derived classes, and are its friends, so a class derived from suite cannot be constructed, and has no access to the state of the suite.
The class is non-copyable and non-movable to preserve unique ownership and consistent state throughout the test session.
